nodes.name: Turning the shoulder
nodes.condition: you want the sword higher or lower
nodes.response: hold a shoulder key, and the arm turns for as long as you hold it

nodes.name: Bending and straightening the elbow
nodes.condition: the target is nearer or farther than your blade
nodes.response: straighten the elbow to reach farther, and bend it to pull the blade in

nodes.name: The sword carries on
nodes.condition: a swing is moving
nodes.response: let go of the key before the blade gets where you want it, because the heavy sword keeps turning the arm

nodes.name: Stepping
nodes.condition: you are too far from your opponent, or too close
nodes.response: hold a step key, and the ground carries you that way while the legs keep you upright

nodes.name: Jumping
nodes.condition: you need to leave the ground
nodes.response: press jump: you get one jump from the ground

nodes.name: The bounce in the air
nodes.condition: you are in the air and still have your second jump
nodes.response: press jump to bounce off the air, holding a direction to push that way; a jump late in a fall rises higher, because the fall turns into a rise at the same speed

nodes.name: Getting up
nodes.condition: you are knocked down and still have both legs
nodes.response: press stand

nodes.name: Dodging
nodes.condition: a blade is about to touch you
nodes.response: press dodge so that the moment no blade can cut you covers the touch; your own blade cuts nothing in that moment either

nodes.name: Rolling
nodes.condition: you want to dodge and change place on the ground
nodes.response: hold a direction as you press dodge

nodes.name: Dodging in the air
nodes.condition: you are in the air and need to get out of the way
nodes.response: press dodge to be carried sideways, at the cost of your second jump

nodes.name: The wait after a dodge
nodes.condition: you dodged a moment ago
nodes.response: expect a short wait before the next dodge, so choose the moment rather than pressing again

nodes.name: Blocking
nodes.condition: a swing is coming at you
nodes.response: put your blade in its path, because swords are solid and a blade that meets yours stops

nodes.name: What a cut is
nodes.condition: your moving blade touches a part of a fighter
nodes.response: the blade cuts straight across that part where it touched, and what lies beyond the cut drops off; a slow blade does not cut

nodes.name: Where a cut ends the round
nodes.condition: you choose where to aim
nodes.response: aim across the neck, the head or the heart, because a cut there ends the round

nodes.name: Ink
nodes.condition: a cut lands somewhere that does not end the round
nodes.response: the stump spills ink until the round ends, faster for a larger cut, and a fighter who runs out of ink loses the round

nodes.name: Swinging for speed
nodes.condition: you need to cross ground fast or leave it
nodes.response: swing in one direction again and again: each swing adds speed to your whole fighter

nodes.name: Planting the sword
nodes.condition: you want to rise or vault
nodes.response: put the tip on the ground and straighten the arm; the sword cannot go into the ground, so the push lifts you

nodes.name: Reach
nodes.condition: the opponent's blade is longer than yours
nodes.response: let them swing first and move in while their blade travels, because a longer, heavier blade is slower to start and to stop

nodes.name: The opening after a committed move
nodes.condition: the opponent has finished a swing, a thrust or a landing
nodes.response: attack in that moment, before they can move again

nodes.name: A path already chosen
nodes.condition: the opponent is in the air or has planted the sword
nodes.response: move to where they are not going, and cut where they land

nodes.name: Getting around a guard
nodes.condition: the opponent holds the sword out in front
nodes.response: go over or under the blade, toward the part it does not cover

nodes.name: Stopping a turning blade
nodes.condition: the opponent keeps the sword turning
nodes.response: meet it with a firm block, then strike while they build speed again

nodes.name: High against low
nodes.condition: an attack comes low, or a guard sits high, or an overhead waits for your jump
nodes.response: answer from the other height: over a sweep, under a high guard, and on the ground against an overhead

nodes.name: Aim where they do not defend
nodes.condition: the opponent dodges attacks at one part of the body
nodes.response: aim at another part that still ends the round or drains it

nodes.name: Drawing a move
nodes.condition: the opponent answers a threat rather than attacking
nodes.response: make the threat, let them answer, and strike as the answer ends

nodes.name: Your own moves returned
nodes.condition: the opponent copies what you did last round
nodes.response: do this round what you know how to answer next round

nodes.name: A late change
nodes.condition: the opponent looks a short time ahead before choosing
nodes.response: start a move that looks harmless and change it late

nodes.name: Inside their reaction
nodes.condition: the opponent reacts some time after you move
nodes.response: finish what you start before they can answer it

nodes.name: Distance
nodes.condition: the opponent keeps away from you, or waits for you to come
nodes.response: close in with your guard up, and keep your blade where they will be

nodes.name: A guard above
nodes.condition: the opponent comes down at you from the air
nodes.response: hold your sword above you, because a blade that meets yours stops

nodes.name: Light gravity
nodes.condition: gravity is weaker than usual
nodes.response: jump later and expect to hang longer, for you and for them

nodes.name: An opponent with more ink
nodes.condition: the opponent has twice your ink
nodes.response: go for a cut that ends the round rather than waiting for them to run dry

nodes.name: Winning a round
nodes.condition: a round starts against an opponent who does not fight back
nodes.response: close the distance and land a cut that ends the round

nodes.name: Winning a match
nodes.condition: an opponent fights back
nodes.response: find what they commit to, answer it, and do that again in the next round

nodes.name: Watch before you commit
nodes.condition: you meet a new opponent
nodes.response: watch what they repeat before you attack

nodes.name: Compare two opponents
nodes.condition: two opponents differ in one thing
nodes.response: find that difference, and change the part of your plan it touches

edges.label: letting go early is the same shoulder key, timed against the weight of the sword
a cut needs a moving blade, and the shoulder is what moves it
a block is the shoulder holding the blade in the path of a swing
speed comes from swinging the shoulder one way
the elbow decides whether the blade reaches the part you aim at
straightening the arm is what pushes the planted tip
reach is your straightened arm measured against theirs
distance is your steps chosen against theirs
a round starts with closing the distance
the second jump is the first with the ground replaced by a bounce
a jump is one way over a low attack
an air dodge spends the second jump
light gravity is the same jump with the fall slowed
a roll is a dodge with a direction held
an air dodge is a dodge with the ground taken away
the wait comes after the dodge
their dodge is the move you learned, used against you, so aim at a part that does not trigger it
the wait after their dodge is the opening a drawn dodge gives you
stopping a turning blade is a block held against something that keeps coming
a guard above is a block against a swing that comes down
a guard that waits is a block you have to go around
meeting a sweep from above is a block from another height
against someone who swings back, your blade is also your shield
a cut that ends the round is an ordinary cut across a different part
a cut that does not end the round still costs ink
an opening is worth something when you have a cut to land in it
if one part that ends the round is defended, another still ends it
a cut that ends the round does not depend on how much ink is left
a round ends with a cut across the neck, the head or the heart
with twice the ink to drain, waiting for them to run dry takes twice as long
a plant is a swing whose push goes into the ground
an opponent who plants has done what you can do, and their path is fixed until they land
a jump or a plant is a committed move that lasts longer
drawing a move makes the opening instead of waiting for it
your own last round is the committed move you face
an opening lasts as long as they take to react
what wins rounds against a real opponent is the opening after what they commit to
looking ahead is reacting early, and a late change lands past what they looked at
a match is rounds won against someone who answers back
watching first shows which moves they commit to
watching your own round is how you see what comes back
comparing two opponents shows what changed, and so where to aim
comparing a fight with and without its condition shows what the condition changes
